Molecular mechanisms of tolerance At the molecular level, several key signaling pathways are involved in establishing maternal-fetal immune tolerance 35. One prominent pathway involves the interaction between KIRs on uNK cells and HLA-C molecules on trophoblasts 16,27,36. This KIR-HLA-C engagement plays a pivotal role in regulating trophoblast invasion and promoting immune tolerance 20,22,32. Certain combinations of maternal KIR and fetal HLA-C genotypes have been associated with more favorable pregnancy outcomes, while others may predispose to complications such as preeclampsia 18,37. Cytokine signaling is another crucial mechanism in immune toler- ance at the maternal-fetal interface 38. uNK cells, along with other immune cells in the decidua, produce cytokines like interleukin-10 IL-10 and transforming growth factor-beta TGF-β , which are essen - tial for maintaining an anti-inflammatory environment conducive to pregnancy 39,40. IL-10 helps suppress pro-inflammatory responses that could harm the fetus, while TGF-β contributes to immune regulation by modulating the function of uNK cells and Tregs 41. These cytokines collectively foster a supportive environment that minimizes maternal immune attacks on fetal cells while enabling immune adaptations that support fetal growth 42. To further illustrate the temporal changes in immune regulation essential for pregnancy, Fig. 2provides an overview of immune cell dynamics across the trimesters, emphasizing the shifts from an initial pro-inflammatory state to an anti-inflammatory phase and finally returning to a pro-inflammatory environment as pregnancy progresses 43. These phases reflect the intricate balance required at the maternal-fetal interface to support implantation, fetal development, and preparation for labor 44. Cytokine and Growth Factor Reviews 81 2025 40 53 422. Role of trophoblasts in tolerance Trophoblasts, specialized cells originating from the outer layer of the blastocyst, play a direct role in immune tolerance at the maternal-fetal interface 22,29,45. These cells differentiate into extravillous tropho - blasts EVTs , which invade the maternal decidua and interact with uNK cells and other maternal immune cells 7,13,46. EVTs express non-classical HLA molecules, including HLA-G, which interacts with inhibitory receptors on uNK cells and Tregs to promote immune toler- ance 47. By doing so, trophoblasts help modulate local immune re- sponses, ensuring that the maternal immune system does not mount an attack against fetal cells while facilitating the necessary remodeling of spiral arteries for optimal placental function 48,49. In summary, maternal-fetal immune tolerance is mediated by a network of immune cells, signaling pathways, and cellular interactions at the maternal-fetal interface. uNK cells, through KIR-HLA-C in- teractions and cytokine production, along with the regulatory functions of trophoblasts, play central roles in maintaining this tolerance 13,20, 27,50. Understanding these mechanisms is crucial for identifying how disruptions in tolerance may lead to pregnancy complications and for developing therapeutic approaches to mitigate these risks 16,18,39. Cellular and molecular mechanisms of uNK cells in pregnancy uNK cells play a critical role in pregnancy by modulating key pro- cesses that support placental development and maternal-fetal immune tolerance 5,51,52.

IFN- γ, released by uNK cells, plays a critical role in regulating trophoblast invasion and pro- moting spiral artery remodeling, primarily through pathways involving nitric oxide and prostaglandin signaling 67. Growth factors and angiogenic signaling The production of growth factors by uNK cells, such as vascular endothelial growth factor VEGF and placental growth factor PlGF , is essential for promoting angiogenesis and vascular remodeling 69. These growth factors facilitate the transformation of spiral arteries, ensuring an increased blood supply to the developing fetus 70. Additionally, uNK cells express angiopoietins, which contribute to vascular stability and maturation, further support - ing the development of a robust maternal-fetal circulation 12,13,71. Through these cellular and molecular mechanisms, uNK cells exert multifaceted effects that are essential for a successful pregnancy 7,40, 53. Pregnancy complications linked to uNK dysfunction Aberrations in uNK cell function have been implicated in several pregnancy complications, with dysfunctional uNK cells contributing to impaired placental development and inadequate maternal-fetal immune tolerance 5,73. This section explores specific pregnancy disorders associated with uNK dysfunction, detailing molecular mechanisms, and the impact of genetic and epigenetic factors on uNK cell function 7,74. Detailed mechanisms 4. Preeclampsia Preeclampsia is a complex pregnancy disorder characterized by high blood pressure and end-organ damage, affecting both maternal and fetal health 75,76.

content_chunk: uNK cells play a crucial role in spiral artery remodeling, which is necessary for establishing an adequate blood supply to the placenta. In preeclampsia, impaired uNK cell function disrupts the secretion of essential angiogenic factors such as vascular endothelial growth factor VEGF and placental growth factor PlGF , resulting in inadequate spiral artery transformation and poor placental perfusion. Additionally, dysfunctional IFN- γ and TNF- α signaling from uNK cells can create an inflammatory environment, further increasing vascular resistance 36,77. The interaction between KIRs on uNK cells and HLA-C on trophoblasts is also significant in preeclampsia, with specific KIR-HLA-C genotypes being linked to an increased risk of this condition 67,78. 4illustrates the molecular pathways involved in uNK- trophoblast interactions to enhance our understanding of how uNK cell dysfunction contributes to pregnancy complications. This visual highlights how variations in cytokine production, signaling pathways, and receptor-ligand interactions influence the processes critical for a healthy pregnancy, such as spiral artery remodeling and immune tolerance. Recurrent pregnancy loss RPL Recurrent pregnancy loss, defined as two or more consecutive pregnancy losses, has been associated with abnormalities in uNK cell populations and function within the decidua 79. Abnormal uNK cell activity can lead to an imbalance in cytokine production, disrupting immune tolerance and supporting an overly aggressive immune response that hinders fetal survival 40,77. Reduced levels of anti-inflammatory cytokines such as IL-10 and TGF- β compromise the immune-protective environment essential for early pregnancy estab - lishment 80,81. Moreover, inadequate KIR-HLA interaction impede proper trophoblast invasion, contributing to placental insufficiency and subsequent pregnancy loss 82. Studies indicate that an altered ratio of CD56bright and CD56dim uNK cells in the decidua could impact immune regulation, further emphasizing the role of uNK cells in maintaining pregnancy 27,83. Placenta accreta spectrum PAS disorders PAS disorders, including placenta accreta, increta, and percreta, involve abnormal invasion of the placenta into the uterine wall 84. uNK cells are essential for controlling trophoblast invasion; however, dysfunctions in uNK cell signaling pathways or cytokine production can lead to either excessive or insufficient trophoblast invasion 6,36,52. Imbalances in matrix metalloproteinases MMPs and their tissue in- hibitors TIMPs , regulated by uNK cells, are implicated in PAS disorders 85. The failure of uNK cells to modulate trophoblast operly can result in excessive tissue invasion, creating complications during delivery due to the inability to separate the placenta from the uterus 53,86. The molecular mechanisms underlying this dysregulation highlight the need for improved diagnostic and therapeutic strategies targeting uNK cell-trophoblast interactions in PAS disorders 19,87. Specific KIR-HLA-C genotypes influence the extent of uNK cell activation, affecting trophoblast invasion and immune tolerance 20, 36.

content_chunk: Applied to uNK cells, scRNA-seq has allowed researchers to identify previously unrecognized subtypes and functional states of these cells at the maternal-fetal interface 97. By analyzing gene expression at the single-cell level, scRNA-seq provides insights into the diversity of uNK cell populations and the specific roles they play throughout different stages of pregnancy 55,98. This technology has proven essential for mapping uNK cell heterogeneity, revealing distinct clusters based on cytokine production, receptor expression, and migratory properties, which contribute to maternal-fetal tolerance and placental development 99. Spatial transcriptomics While scRNA-seq provides detailed transcriptional profiles, it does not retain spatial information, which is crucial for understanding the functional context of cells within the tissue architecture. Spatial tran- scriptomics addresses this limitation by combining gene expression analysis with spatial localization, allowing researchers to examine how uNK cells are distributed and interact within the decidua 100. This technique offers a spatially resolved view of uNK cell heterogeneity, showing how specific subtypes cluster around trophoblast cells and blood vessels, thereby contributing to trophoblast invasion, spiral artery remodeling, and immune modulation. Spatial transcriptomics thus provides insights into how the tissue microenvironment influences uNK cell behavior 55,101. Molecular pathways of uNK-trophoblast interactions. Understanding uNK cell heterogeneity and function These emerging techniques have deepened our understanding of uNK cell heterogeneity, revealing complex functional distinctions among various uNK subtypes 14. For instance, combining scRNA-seq with spatial transcriptomics has highlighted differences in cytokine expression between CD56bright and CD56dim uNK cells, with implications for their distinct roles in immune regulation and placental development 55,104. Understanding these nuanced differences is crucial for eluci- dating the mechanisms by which uNK cells contribute to maternal-fetal tolerance and pregnancy health 59. Implications for clinical research and therapeutic development The application of these techniques extends beyond basic research, offering promising avenues for clinical translation. By identifying spe- cific uNK cell subtypes and pathways associated with pregnancy com- plications, these methods enable the development of targeted therapies aimed at modulating uNK cell function 25,53. For example, scRNA-seq data can inform potential biomarkers for early diagnosis of disorders like preeclampsia or recurrent pregnancy loss, while spatial transcriptomics may reveal critical microenvironmental factors that could be targeted to enhance uNK cell function 106. Advanced imaging techniques could also aid in evaluating the efficacy of novel therapeutics by visualizing their effects on uNK cell distribution and activity within the uterine environment 107. In summary, cutting-edge techniques such as single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and advanced imaging are trans - forming uNK cell research 108. By providing comprehensive insights into uNK cell heterogeneity and interactions within the decidua, these tools not only enhance our understanding of maternal-fetal immune tolerance but also pave the way for novel diagnostic and therapeutic strategies for managing pregnancy-related complications 5,104. Therapeutic targets and potential interventions The critical roles of uNK cells in maintaining maternal-fetal immune tolerance, supporting placental development, and modulating immune responses underscore their potential as therapeutic targets 5,7,109. Advances in understanding uNK cell function and their interactions with trophoblasts and other immune cells have paved the way for exploring therapeutic strategies aimed at modulating uNK activity 24,53. This section provides an overview of current and prospective therapies tar- geting uNK cell function, cytokine modulation, gene therapy, and monoclonal antibodies mAbs , along with relevant clinical trials and preclinical models. Current and prospective therapeutics 6. uNK cell function modulation Directly targeting uNK cell function offers an avenue for improving pregnancy outcomes in patients at risk of complications related to uNK dysfunction 110. Strategies focusing on enhancing or suppressing uNK activity could potentially correct the imbalance that contributes to conditions like preeclampsia and recurrent pregnancy loss 36,111. Small molecule inhibitors or activators that modulate uNK cell cyto- toxicity, cytokine production, or adhesion are promising approaches, yet they pose risks of unintended immune effects. For instance, excessive modulation of IFN-γ could either exacerbate inflammation or, if overly suppressed, reduce immune surveillance, potentially compromising maternal-fetal tolerance 11,112.

content_chunk: Cytokine modulation Cytokine signaling is vital for uNK cell function, with specific cyto- kines such as IL-10, TGF-β, and VEGF playing essential roles in main - taining immune tolerance and supporting angiogenesis 63,113. Therapeutic modulation of these cytokines has been proposed to restore balance in uNK-mediated immune responses. However, achieving pre- cise control over cytokine levels is challenging. Exogenously delivered IL-10 and TGF-β, for instance, may enhance an anti-inflammatory environment but carry risks of immune suppression, which could in- crease susceptibility to infections or other immune-related complica - tions 114. Additionally, VEGF-based therapies aimed at promoting placental vascularization may inadvertently promote abnormal vascular growth if not carefully controlled, raising concerns about potential im- pacts on placental structure and function 115. Gene therapy Gene-editing technologies such as CRISPR-Cas9 present promising opportunities to correct genetic variations influencing uNK cell function, specifically by modifying genes like KIR and HLA-C to optimize uNK cell-trophoblast interactions 116. While gene therapy holds potential for preventing complications arising from genetic imbalances, this approach also introduces significant ethical and safety concerns, particularly in the context of pregnancy 117. There is a risk of off-target effects, which could lead to unintended genetic changes with unpredictable impacts on both maternal and fetal health. Rigorous preclinical studies are essential to ensure the feasibility and safety of gene-editing interventions in pregnancy 118. Monoclonal antibodies Monoclonal antibody mAb therapies targeting specific pathways involved in uNK cell function offer another innovative therapeutic avenue 119. mAbs designed to modulate KIR-HLA-C interactions could theoretically enhance maternal-fetal tolerance by fine-tuning uNK cell activity 64,120. Additionally, antibodies targeting pro-inflammatory cytokines like TNF- α may help manage inflammation-related preg- nancy complications 121. Despite promising preclinical results, mAb therapies must be carefully evaluated for potential impacts on maternal-fetal immune dynamics. Safety profiles need to be rigorously tested to prevent unintended immune reactions that might disrupt the delicate balance of tolerance required during pregnancy 122. content_chunk: Addi- tionally, clinical trials on cytokine therapy in autoimmune or inflam - matory conditions may serve as models for pregnancy-specific interventions, although uNK-targeted therapies for pregnancy compli - cations remain limited 22,132. Preclinical models Animal models, particularly murine and rat models, have been invaluable in studying uNK cell function and potential interventions 133. Knockout models lacking specific genes like those encoding KIRs or cytokines e. , IL-10, TGF- β provide insights into how these mole- cules influence uNK cell function and pregnancy outcomes 7,50,104. Advances in humanized mouse models, where human uNK cells are introduced into immunocompromised mice, also offer new avenues for testing therapeutic interventions in a controlled environment 134. In summary, a variety of therapeutic strategies targeting uNK cell function, cytokine modulation, gene therapy, and mAbs are being explored for managing pregnancy complications associated with uNK dysfunction 135. Although still in early stages, these approaches hold promise for improving pregnancy outcomes by enhancing maternal-fetal immune tolerance and supporting placental health 136. Further clin- ical trials and refined preclinical models are essential to translate these therapeutic concepts into safe and effective treatments, ultimately aiming to optimize maternal-fetal immune interactions and promote healthy placental function 137. Future directions and knowledge gaps Significant advancements have been made in understanding the roles of uNK cells in maternal-fetal immune tolerance, yet critical knowledge gaps persist. Addressing these gaps is essential for a more comprehensive understanding of pregnancy complications associated with uNK cell dysfunction and could pave the way for novel therapeutic strategies. This section highlights key research needs and explores the potential for biomarker development and personalized interventions. Highlight research needs 7. Understanding uNK cell subtypes and their functions Although various uNK cell subtypes have been identified, such as CD56bright CD16dim and CD56dimt CD16bright, their precise functions and interactions within the uterine environment remain incompletely un- derstood 61,138. Each subtype appears to play distinct roles, including regulatory, angiogenic, or immune defense functions, yet how these roles evolve throughout pregnancy is still unclear 52,53,139. Detailed studies are necessary to elucidate how each uNK subtype contributes to placental development and immune tolerance, especially in high-risk pregnancies. Influence of environmental and maternal factors Environmental and lifestyle factors, including diet, stress, infection, and exposure to toxins, can impact maternal immune function and potentially alter uNK cell behavior 140. However, limited research has focused on how these external factors influence uNK cell function and interactions with trophoblasts 13,22,104. Furthermore, maternal health conditions, such as autoimmune disorders and metabolic syn- dromes, may affect uNK cells and exacerbate pregnancy complications 141. Future studies should explore the environmental and maternal factors affecting uNK cell functions and assess how these influences vary across populations with different genetic backgrounds. Longitudinal changes in uNK cells during pregnancy Most current research on uNK cells is limited to early pregnancy stages, with fewer studies examining their roles in mid-to-late pregnancy 142. Understanding the dynamic changes in uNK cell populations, phenotypes, and functions throughout pregnancy is essential for iden- tifying how they contribute to pregnancy maintenance and how dysre - gulation may lead to complications 143. Longitudinal studies tracking uNK cell characteristics from conception to delivery could reveal crucial insights into their temporal roles and adaptation within the uterine environment 52,104,144. Mechanistic pathways beyond KIR-HLA-C interactions While the KIR-HLA-C axis is well-studied in maternal-fetal tolerance, other molecular pathways may significantly influence uNK cell function 7,145. Pathways involving cytokines like IL-15, IL-10, and TGF-β, as well as non-HLA ligand-receptor interactions, have been suggested to influence uNK cell activity 7,146.

content_chunk: Further research into these less-studied pathways may reveal additional mechanisms that support immune tolerance and placental health, expanding our understanding of the immune microenvironment in pregnancy. Potential for biomarkers and personalized interventions 7. Development of non-invasive biomarkers Identifying biomarkers indicative of uNK cell activity could facilitate early detection of pregnancy complications, such as preeclampsia and recurrent pregnancy loss 21,40. Non-invasive biomarkers, particularly those detectable in maternal blood or urine, would offer clinicians a valuable tool for assessing uNK cell function and associated risks throughout pregnancy 147. Potential biomarkers may include cyto- kines, chemokines, and uNK-specific surface markers that correlate with abnormal immune responses 148. Validation of these biomarkers in large, diverse populations is essential to ensure their reliability and predictive accuracy. Potential for personalized interventions The diversity in uNK cell subtypes and their distinct roles in immune tolerance and placental support suggest a strong potential for person - alized approaches to treating pregnancy complications 149. Person - alized interventions could involve targeted modulation of specific uNK subtypes, or the use of cytokine therapies tailored to an individual s immune profile. For example, regulating cytokines, such as IL-10 or VEGF, based on a patient s specific needs could enhance treatment ef- ficacy by precisely addressing immune imbalances 150. Additionally, genetic screening for KIR-HLA mismatches may help identify women at higher risk for complications, allowing for early, targeted interventions aimed at improving maternal-fetal compatibility 151. Future research should prioritize developing these targeted therapies, focusing on ac- commodating individual variations in immune tolerance mechanisms to maximize therapeutic outcomes 21,152. Personalized approaches offer the promise of more effective, patient-specific care that addresses the unique immune environment of each pregnancy. In summary, advancing our understanding of uNK cells requires a multifaceted approach that includes studies on cellular diversity, environmental impacts, and longitudinal dynamics. Developing reliable biomarkers and personalized therapeutic strategies holds great promise for improving pregnancy outcomes and managing complications linked to uNK dysfunction 153. Bridging these knowledge gaps will be critical for translating basic research on uNK cells into clinical applications, ultimately enhancing maternal-fetal health 36,40. Conclusions and prospects 8. Summary of key insights This review has highlighted the multifaceted role of uNK cells in establishing and maintaining maternal-fetal immune tolerance, ensuring successful placental development, and supporting pregnancy health 7, 53. uNK cells contribute significantly to processes such as trophoblast invasion, spiral artery remodeling, and modulation of immune responses at the maternal-fetal interface 7,13,154. Their interaction with trophoblast cells, mediated through KIR-HLA-C and other molecular pathways, is essential for balancing immune tolerance and defense, thereby preventing adverse pregnancy outcomes 20,27. Additionally, the functional diversity of uNK cell subtypes, characterized by unique cytokine profiles and receptor expressions, underscores the complexity of their regulatory roles 63,77. Understanding the implications of uNK cell dysfunction has provided valuable insights into pregnancy complications, including preeclampsia, recurrent pregnancy loss, and PAS disorders 12,77. Genetic and epigenetic factors that influence uNK cell activity have also emerged as critical determinants of maternal-fetal tolerance, revealing potential risk markers for these conditions 7,55,145.

content_chunk: Advances in research tech- niques, particularly single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial tran- scriptomics, have further enhanced our understanding of uNK cell heterogeneity, opening up new avenues for targeted therapeutic ap- proaches 155. Potential clinical impact and future research The clinical implications of uNK cell research are vast, particularly in developing predictive biomarkers and personalized therapies for preg- nancy complications 104,156. Non-invasive biomarkers reflecting uNK cell activity could transform prenatal care by enabling early detection and intervention for high-risk pregnancies 157. Such bio- markers, combined with genetic screening for KIR-HLA mismatches, may facilitate individualized risk assessments, helping to tailor in- terventions for each patient s unique immunological profile 7,55,66. Future research should focus on exploring uncharted areas in uNK cell biology including their longitudinal behavior across different pregnancy stages and the influence of environmental factors 52,158. These studies could deepen our understanding of how uNK cells adapt to changes within the uterine environment and contribute to pregnancy maintenance over time. Further exploration into alternative ligand-receptor pathways and cytokine interactions will likely reveal additional layers of immune regulation essential for pregnancy health 159. In conclusion, recent advancements in uNK cell research have significantly expanded our understanding of their roles and interactions with trophoblasts 7,22,50,53. Despite remaining gaps in knowledge, these findings highlight the transformative potential of uNK cell research in reproductive immunology and maternal-fetal medicine 160. By continuing to explore molecular mechanisms and the impact of various factors on uNK cell functions, paving the way for innovative diagnostic tools, targeted treatments, and ultimately, improved preg- nancy outcomes. Cytokine modulation and immunoregulation of uterine NK cells in pregnancy disorders Jun Zhoua, Ping Yanb, Wenxue Mac, , Jing Lia, aDepartment of Obstetrics, The Affiliated Hospital of Qingdao University, Qingdao, Shandong 266000, China bQingdao City Health Care Center for Cadres, Qingdao, Shandong 266071, China cDivision of Regenerative Medicine, Department of Medicine, Sanford Stem Cell Institute, University of California San Diego, La Jolla, CA 92093, USA Keywords: Cytokine modulation Growth factor signaling Uterine natural killer uNK cells Immune tolerance KIR-HLA-C interaction Pregnancy complicationsABSTRACT Uterine natural killer uNK cells play a pivotal role in promoting placental development and supporting maternal-fetal immune tolerance, primarily through cytokine regulation and growth factor production. While the importance of uNK cells in pregnancy is well-established, the mechanisms of their interactions with trophoblasts and contributions to various pregnancy complications remain incompletely understood. This review highlights recent advancements in understanding uNK cell functions, with a focus on cytokine production, growth factor secretion, and receptor-ligand interactions, particularly involving killer immunoglobulin-like receptors KIR and human leukocyte antigen-C HLA-C. We explore how uNK cell dysfunction contributes to pregnancy compli - cations, including preeclampsia, recurrent pregnancy loss, and placenta accreta spectrum PAS disorders, emphasizing their roles in immune tolerance and placental health. By detailing the distinct cytokine signaling pathways and functional subtypes of uNK cells, this review provides insights into their regulatory mechanisms essential for pregnancy maintenance. Additionally, we discuss emerging therapeutic strategies targeting uNK- trophoblast interactions and propose future research directions, including the development of non-invasive biomarkers and personalized interventions. This comprehensive review addresses critical knowledge gaps, aiming to advance research in reproductive immunology and guide therapeutic innovations in maternal health. Introduction The placenta is a vital organ that forms during pregnancy, acting as the interface between the mother and the developing fetus 1. It is essential for exchanging nutrients, gases, and waste products, which supports fetal growth and development 2. The placenta comprises various cell types, including trophoblasts, specialized cells derived from the outer layer of the blastocyst 3. Trophoblasts invade the maternal uterine wall to establish the placenta, a process essential for successful pregnancy outcomes 4. Since their identification, uterine natural killer uNK cells have been recognized as key regulators in maintaining maternal-fetal immune tolerance 5. Unlike peripheral NK cells, uNK cells exhibit limited cytotoxicity and are highly adapted to the pregnancy environment, promoting processes such as trophoblast invasion, spiral artery remod - eling, and immune modulation 6. These cells play a crucial role in balancing maternal immune tolerance with immune defense, making them essential players in pregnancy. Recent advances highlight diverse uNK cell subtypes, each with specific roles in supporting fetal develop - ment within the maternal immune environment 7. Placental development involves several key stages, starting with the differentiation of cytotrophoblasts into syncytiotrophoblasts, which form the outer layer of the placenta 8.

Additionally, it explores the association of uNK cell dysfunction with pregnancy complications and the potential of thera - peutic strategies targeting uNK-trophoblast interactions 21. This exploration serves as a bridge between basic research and clinical ap- plications, guiding future studies on therapeutic interventions and biomarker development. This article is structured to provide a comprehensive understanding of uNK cells within the broader context of maternal-fetal immune tolerance 5,7,11. It begins by reviewing foundational mechanisms of immune tolerance during pregnancy, including key cellular and mo- lecular players involved 22. Following this, the specific functions of uNK cells are explored, with an emphasis on their subtypes and roles in supporting placental development 12,23. The potential impacts of uNK cell dysfunction on pregnancy complications are then discussed, including associated mechanisms and genetic predispositions 11. Emerging techniques, such as single-cell RNA sequencing, are high- lighted for their contributions to advancing our understanding of uNK cell heterogeneity 21,24. Finally, the manuscript examines current and prospective therapeutic strategies targeting uNK cell functions and concludes with a summary of key insights and future research directions in this field 7,25. In summary, studying placental immune interactions, particularly the role of uNK cells, is crucial for understanding and managing preg- nancy outcomes 7,11. Recent advances have provided significant in- sights into these interactions, highlighting their complexity and importance 7,26,27. This review aims to synthesize current knowledge, identify gaps, and suggest future research directions, mak- ing a valuable contribution to reproductive immunology and maternal-fetal medicine 11,28. Maternal-fetal immune tolerances Achieving immune tolerance at the maternal-fetal interface is essential for a successful pregnancy, requiring a finely tuned balance between immune defense and tolerance 22,29. This section explores the key components and processes that establish and maintain this balance, beginning with an overview of the immune tolerance mecha - nisms in place during pregnancy 30. Overview of immune tolerance mechanisms The establishment and maintenance of immune tolerance at the maternal-fetal interface are critical for a successful pregnancy. Maternal immune tolerance involves a complex interplay of cellular and molec - ular components that allow the maternal immune system to accept the semi-allogeneic fetus while preserving the ability to defend against in- fections 31. A key player in this process is the uNK cell, which, unlike peripheral NK cells, exhibits reduced cytotoxicity and is adapted to promote tolerance and support placental development 12,13,32. Additionally, other immune cells, including macrophages, dendritic cells DCs , and T regulatory cells Tregs , contribute to a balanced immune environment that facilitates fetal development 33. Each of these cell types produces cytokines, growth factors, and other mediators that support the delicate balance between immune tolerance and de- fense within the uterine environment 34. Molecular mechanisms of tolerance At the molecular level, several key signaling pathways are involved in establishing maternal-fetal immune tolerance 35. One prominent pathway involves the interaction between KIRs on uNK cells and HLA-C molecules on trophoblasts 16,27,36. This KIR-HLA-C engagement plays a pivotal role in regulating trophoblast invasion and promoting immune tolerance 20,22,32. Certain combinations of maternal KIR and fetal HLA-C genotypes have been associated with more favorable pregnancy outcomes, while others may predispose to complications such as preeclampsia 18,37. Cytokine signaling is another crucial mechanism in immune toler- ance at the maternal-fetal interface 38. uNK cells, along with other immune cells in the decidua, produce cytokines like interleukin-10 IL-10 and transforming growth factor-beta TGF-β , which are essen - tial for maintaining an anti-inflammatory environment conducive to pregnancy 39,40. IL-10 helps suppress pro-inflammatory responses that could harm the fetus, while TGF-β contributes to immune regulation by modulating the function of uNK cells and Tregs 41. These cytokines collectively foster a supportive environment that minimizes maternal immune attacks on fetal cells while enabling immune adaptations that support fetal growth 42. To further illustrate the temporal changes in immune regulation essential for pregnancy, Fig. 2provides an overview of immune cell dynamics across the trimesters, emphasizing the shifts from an initial pro-inflammatory state to an anti-inflammatory phase and finally returning to a pro-inflammatory environment as pregnancy progresses 43. These phases reflect the intricate balance required at the maternal-fetal interface to support implantation, fetal development, and preparation for labor 44. Cytokine and Growth Factor Reviews 81 2025 40 53 422. Role of trophoblasts in tolerance Trophoblasts, specialized cells originating from the outer layer of the blastocyst, play a direct role in immune tolerance at the maternal-fetal interface 22,29,45. These cells differentiate into extravillous tropho - blasts EVTs , which invade the maternal decidua and interact with uNK cells and other maternal immune cells 7,13,46. EVTs express non-classical HLA molecules, including HLA-G, which interacts with inhibitory receptors on uNK cells and Tregs to promote immune toler- ance 47. By doing so, trophoblasts help modulate local immune re- sponses, ensuring that the maternal immune system does not mount an attack against fetal cells while facilitating the necessary remodeling of spiral arteries for optimal placental function 48,49. In summary, maternal-fetal immune tolerance is mediated by a network of immune cells, signaling pathways, and cellular interactions at the maternal-fetal interface. uNK cells, through KIR-HLA-C in- teractions and cytokine production, along with the regulatory functions of trophoblasts, play central roles in maintaining this tolerance 13,20, 27,50. Understanding these mechanisms is crucial for identifying how disruptions in tolerance may lead to pregnancy complications and for developing therapeutic approaches to mitigate these risks 16,18,39. Cellular and molecular mechanisms of uNK cells in pregnancy uNK cells play a critical role in pregnancy by modulating key pro- cesses that support placental development and maternal-fetal immune tolerance 5,51,52.

CD56brightCD16dim uNK cells This subtype represents the majority of uNK cells in the decidua during early pregnancy and is primarily responsible for cytokine and growth factor production rather than direct cytotoxicity 55,56. CD56dim uNK cells may contribute to immune surveillance, acting as a defense mechanism against potential infections during pregnancy 60. How- ever, their role remains more restrained, focusing on regulatory functions and maintaining a balanced immune response 39,58.

KIR-HLA-C interactions The engagement of killer immunoglobulin-like receptors KIRs on uNK cells with human leukocyte antigen-C HLA-C on trophoblasts is central to regulating trophoblast invasion and maintaining maternal- fetal tolerance 11,63,64. Specific combinations of maternal KIR and fetal HLA-C alleles influence the extent of trophoblast invasion and are associated with various pregnancy outcomes 22. or instance, certain KIR-HLA-C genotypes promote a more invasive trophoblast phenotype, facilitating deeper placental embedding and improved vascular adap- tation. Conversely, mismatches in these genotypes can lead to inade - quate uNK-trophoblast interactions, contributing to complications such as preeclampsia and recurrent pregnancy loss 65,66. This interaction underscores the importance of genetic compatibility in promoting optimal uNK cell function during pregnancy. IFN- γ, released by uNK cells, plays a critical role in regulating trophoblast invasion and pro- moting spiral artery remodeling, primarily through pathways involving nitric oxide and prostaglandin signaling 67. This cytokine supports vascular changes necessary for adequate placental function. Addition - ally, IL-8 and IL-10 are essential for creating an environment that bal- ances trophoblast invasion with immune tolerance, which is vital for healthy placental development 48,68.

Growth factors and angiogenic signaling The production of growth factors by uNK cells, such as vascular endothelial growth factor VEGF and placental growth factor PlGF , is essential for promoting angiogenesis and vascular remodeling 69. These growth factors facilitate the transformation of spiral arteries, ensuring an increased blood supply to the developing fetus 70. Additionally, uNK cells express angiopoietins, which contribute to vascular stability and maturation, further support - ing the development of a robust maternal-fetal circulation 12,13,71. Through these cellular and molecular mechanisms, uNK cells exert multifaceted effects that are essential for a successful pregnancy 7,40, 53. The diversity in uNK cell subtypes and their signaling interactions highlights the complexity of immune regulation at the maternal-fetal interface 72. Further understanding of these pathways could provide insights into therapeutic strategies for managing pregnancy-related complications. Pregnancy complications linked to uNK dysfunction Aberrations in uNK cell function have been implicated in several pregnancy complications, with dysfunctional uNK cells contributing to impaired placental development and inadequate maternal-fetal immune tolerance 5,73. This section explores specific pregnancy disorders associated with uNK dysfunction, detailing molecular mechanisms, and the impact of genetic and epigenetic factors on uNK cell function 7,74. Detailed mechanisms 4. Preeclampsia Preeclampsia is a complex pregnancy disorder characterized by high blood pressure and end-organ damage, affecting both maternal and fetal health 75,76.

content_chunk: uNK cells play a crucial role in spiral artery remodeling, which is necessary for establishing an adequate blood supply to the placenta. In preeclampsia, impaired uNK cell function disrupts the secretion of essential angiogenic factors such as vascular endothelial growth factor VEGF and placental growth factor PlGF , resulting in inadequate spiral artery transformation and poor placental perfusion. Additionally, dysfunctional IFN- γ and TNF- α signaling from uNK cells can create an inflammatory environment, further increasing vascular resistance 36,77. The interaction between KIRs on uNK cells and HLA-C on trophoblasts is also significant in preeclampsia, with specific KIR-HLA-C genotypes being linked to an increased risk of this condition 67,78. 4illustrates the molecular pathways involved in uNK- trophoblast interactions to enhance our understanding of how uNK cell dysfunction contributes to pregnancy complications. This visual highlights how variations in cytokine production, signaling pathways, and receptor-ligand interactions influence the processes critical for a healthy pregnancy, such as spiral artery remodeling and immune tolerance. Recurrent pregnancy loss RPL Recurrent pregnancy loss, defined as two or more consecutive pregnancy losses, has been associated with abnormalities in uNK cell populations and function within the decidua 79. Abnormal uNK cell activity can lead to an imbalance in cytokine production, disrupting immune tolerance and supporting an overly aggressive immune response that hinders fetal survival 40,77. Reduced levels of anti-inflammatory cytokines such as IL-10 and TGF- β compromise the immune-protective environment essential for early pregnancy estab - lishment 80,81. Moreover, inadequate KIR-HLA interaction impede proper trophoblast invasion, contributing to placental insufficiency and subsequent pregnancy loss 82. Studies indicate that an altered ratio of CD56bright and CD56dim uNK cells in the decidua could impact immune regulation, further emphasizing the role of uNK cells in maintaining pregnancy 27,83. Placenta accreta spectrum PAS disorders PAS disorders, including placenta accreta, increta, and percreta, involve abnormal invasion of the placenta into the uterine wall 84. uNK cells are essential for controlling trophoblast invasion; however, dysfunctions in uNK cell signaling pathways or cytokine production can lead to either excessive or insufficient trophoblast invasion 6,36,52. Imbalances in matrix metalloproteinases MMPs and their tissue in- hibitors TIMPs , regulated by uNK cells, are implicated in PAS disorders 85. The failure of uNK cells to modulate trophoblast operly can result in excessive tissue invasion, creating complications during delivery due to the inability to separate the placenta from the uterus 53,86. The molecular mechanisms underlying this dysregulation highlight the need for improved diagnostic and therapeutic strategies targeting uNK cell-trophoblast interactions in PAS disorders 19,87. Specific KIR-HLA-C genotypes influence the extent of uNK cell activation, affecting trophoblast invasion and immune tolerance 20, 36.

content_chunk: Applied to uNK cells, scRNA-seq has allowed researchers to identify previously unrecognized subtypes and functional states of these cells at the maternal-fetal interface 97. By analyzing gene expression at the single-cell level, scRNA-seq provides insights into the diversity of uNK cell populations and the specific roles they play throughout different stages of pregnancy 55,98. This technology has proven essential for mapping uNK cell heterogeneity, revealing distinct clusters based on cytokine production, receptor expression, and migratory properties, which contribute to maternal-fetal tolerance and placental development 99. Spatial transcriptomics While scRNA-seq provides detailed transcriptional profiles, it does not retain spatial information, which is crucial for understanding the functional context of cells within the tissue architecture. Spatial tran- scriptomics addresses this limitation by combining gene expression analysis with spatial localization, allowing researchers to examine how uNK cells are distributed and interact within the decidua 100. This technique offers a spatially resolved view of uNK cell heterogeneity, showing how specific subtypes cluster around trophoblast cells and blood vessels, thereby contributing to trophoblast invasion, spiral artery remodeling, and immune modulation. Spatial transcriptomics thus provides insights into how the tissue microenvironment influences uNK cell behavior 55,101. Molecular pathways of uNK-trophoblast interactions. IFN- γ released by uNK cells promotes spiral artery remodeling through the pro- duction of nitric oxide, other vasoactive substances, and PGE2 signaling. Through KIR-HLA-C interactions with trophoblasts, uNK cells modulate responses that either support trophoblast invasion and maternal-fetal tolerance, conducive to a successful pregnancy, or activate cytotoxicity, which can contribute to pregnancy com- plications such as abortion or recurrent miscarriage. TGF- α plays a role in promoting an inflammatory immune response during the early trimester, essential for pregnancy initiation. During the middle and late trimesters, TGF- α modulates immune responses to prevent excessive inflammation, balancing immune tolerance to support fetal development. Potential for translational research 5. Understanding uNK cell heterogeneity and function These emerging techniques have deepened our understanding of uNK cell heterogeneity, revealing complex functional distinctions among various uNK subtypes 14. For instance, combining scRNA-seq with spatial transcriptomics has highlighted differences in cytokine expression between CD56bright and CD56dim uNK cells, with implications for their distinct roles in immune regulation and placental development 55,104. Understanding these nuanced differences is crucial for eluci- dating the mechanisms by which uNK cells contribute to maternal-fetal tolerance and pregnancy health 59. Implications for clinical research and therapeutic development The application of these techniques extends beyond basic research, offering promising avenues for clinical translation. By identifying spe- cific uNK cell subtypes and pathways associated with pregnancy com- plications, these methods enable the development of targeted therapies aimed at modulating uNK cell function 25,53. For example, scRNA-seq data can inform potential biomarkers for early diagnosis of disorders like preeclampsia or recurrent pregnancy loss, while spatial transcriptomics may reveal critical microenvironmental factors that could be targeted to enhance uNK cell function 106. Advanced imaging techniques could also aid in evaluating the efficacy of novel therapeutics by visualizing their effects on uNK cell distribution and activity within the uterine environment 107. In summary, cutting-edge techniques such as single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and advanced imaging are trans - forming uNK cell research 108. By providing comprehensive insights into uNK cell heterogeneity and interactions within the decidua, these tools not only enhance our understanding of maternal-fetal immune tolerance but also pave the way for novel diagnostic and therapeutic strategies for managing pregnancy-related complications 5,104. Therapeutic targets and potential interventions The critical roles of uNK cells in maintaining maternal-fetal immune tolerance, supporting placental development, and modulating immune responses underscore their potential as therapeutic targets 5,7,109. Advances in understanding uNK cell function and their interactions with trophoblasts and other immune cells have paved the way for exploring therapeutic strategies aimed at modulating uNK activity 24,53. This section provides an overview of current and prospective therapies tar- geting uNK cell function, cytokine modulation, gene therapy, and monoclonal antibodies mAbs , along with relevant clinical trials and preclinical models. Current and prospective therapeutics 6. uNK cell function modulation Directly targeting uNK cell function offers an avenue for improving pregnancy outcomes in patients at risk of complications related to uNK dysfunction 110. Strategies focusing on enhancing or suppressing uNK activity could potentially correct the imbalance that contributes to conditions like preeclampsia and recurrent pregnancy loss 36,111. Small molecule inhibitors or activators that modulate uNK cell cyto- toxicity, cytokine production, or adhesion are promising approaches, yet they pose risks of unintended immune effects. For instance, excessive modulation of IFN-γ could either exacerbate inflammation or, if overly suppressed, reduce immune surveillance, potentially compromising maternal-fetal tolerance 11,112.

content_chunk: Cytokine modulation Cytokine signaling is vital for uNK cell function, with specific cyto- kines such as IL-10, TGF-β, and VEGF playing essential roles in main - taining immune tolerance and supporting angiogenesis 63,113. Therapeutic modulation of these cytokines has been proposed to restore balance in uNK-mediated immune responses. However, achieving pre- cise control over cytokine levels is challenging. Exogenously delivered IL-10 and TGF-β, for instance, may enhance an anti-inflammatory environment but carry risks of immune suppression, which could in- crease susceptibility to infections or other immune-related complica - tions 114. Additionally, VEGF-based therapies aimed at promoting placental vascularization may inadvertently promote abnormal vascular growth if not carefully controlled, raising concerns about potential im- pacts on placental structure and function 115. Gene therapy Gene-editing technologies such as CRISPR-Cas9 present promising opportunities to correct genetic variations influencing uNK cell function, specifically by modifying genes like KIR and HLA-C to optimize uNK cell-trophoblast interactions 116. While gene therapy holds potential for preventing complications arising from genetic imbalances, this approach also introduces significant ethical and safety concerns, particularly in the context of pregnancy 117. There is a risk of off-target effects, which could lead to unintended genetic changes with unpredictable impacts on both maternal and fetal health. Rigorous preclinical studies are essential to ensure the feasibility and safety of gene-editing interventions in pregnancy 118. Monoclonal antibodies Monoclonal antibody mAb therapies targeting specific pathways involved in uNK cell function offer another innovative therapeutic avenue 119. mAbs designed to modulate KIR-HLA-C interactions could theoretically enhance maternal-fetal tolerance by fine-tuning uNK cell activity 64,120. Additionally, antibodies targeting pro-inflammatory cytokines like TNF- α may help manage inflammation-related preg- nancy complications 121. Despite promising preclinical results, mAb therapies must be carefully evaluated for potential impacts on maternal-fetal immune dynamics. Safety profiles need to be rigorously tested to prevent unintended immune reactions that might disrupt the delicate balance of tolerance required during pregnancy 122. To provide a comprehensive overview of therapeutic strategies tar- geting uNK cell function, cytokine modulation, gene therapy, and anti- body interventions, Fig. 5illustrates these approaches and their mechanisms of action. This figure serves as a visual summary of the therapeutic concepts discussed, followed by Table 2, which details the potential strategies and their status in research or clinical trials. Clinical trials and preclinical models 6. Relevant clinical trials Several clinical trials have been conducted or are ongoing to evaluate therapies that could indirectly influence uNK cell function and maternal- fetal tolerance 5,59. For instance, trials assessing the use of anti-inflammatory agents in managing preeclampsia may offer insights J. content_chunk: Addi- tionally, clinical trials on cytokine therapy in autoimmune or inflam - matory conditions may serve as models for pregnancy-specific interventions, although uNK-targeted therapies for pregnancy compli - cations remain limited 22,132. Preclinical models Animal models, particularly murine and rat models, have been invaluable in studying uNK cell function and potential interventions 133. Knockout models lacking specific genes like those encoding KIRs or cytokines e. , IL-10, TGF- β provide insights into how these mole- cules influence uNK cell function and pregnancy outcomes 7,50,104. Advances in humanized mouse models, where human uNK cells are introduced into immunocompromised mice, also offer new avenues for testing therapeutic interventions in a controlled environment 134. In summary, a variety of therapeutic strategies targeting uNK cell function, cytokine modulation, gene therapy, and mAbs are being explored for managing pregnancy complications associated with uNK dysfunction 135. Although still in early stages, these approaches hold promise for improving pregnancy outcomes by enhancing maternal-fetal immune tolerance and supporting placental health 136. Further clin- ical trials and refined preclinical models are essential to translate these therapeutic concepts into safe and effective treatments, ultimately aiming to optimize maternal-fetal immune interactions and promote healthy placental function 137. Future directions and knowledge gaps Significant advancements have been made in understanding the roles of uNK cells in maternal-fetal immune tolerance, yet critical knowledge gaps persist. Addressing these gaps is essential for a more comprehensive understanding of pregnancy complications associated with uNK cell dysfunction and could pave the way for novel therapeutic strategies. This section highlights key research needs and explores the potential for biomarker development and personalized interventions. Highlight research needs 7. Understanding uNK cell subtypes and their functions Although various uNK cell subtypes have been identified, such as CD56bright CD16dim and CD56dimt CD16bright, their precise functions and interactions within the uterine environment remain incompletely un- derstood 61,138. Each subtype appears to play distinct roles, including regulatory, angiogenic, or immune defense functions, yet how these roles evolve throughout pregnancy is still unclear 52,53,139. Detailed studies are necessary to elucidate how each uNK subtype contributes to placental development and immune tolerance, especially in high-risk pregnancies. Therapeutic approaches targeting uNK cells and immune modulation in pregnancy. A uNK cell function modulation: Strategies include 1 NK-specific chemokine activation, 2 immune checkpoint inhibition e. , PD-1, CTLA-4 , 3 receptor activation e. , CD16 , 4 adoptive transfer of modified cells e. , CAR-NK cells , 5 cytokine recruitment e. , IL-2 , and 6 tri-specific NK engagers for precise modulation. B Cytokine modulation: IL-10 and TGF- β support immune tolerance, while VEGF promotes placental vascularization. C Gene and antibody therapy: Gene-editing e. , CRISPR modifies KIR and HLA-C genes to optimize uNK-trophoblast interactions, with antibody therapies targeting these pathways for improved tolerance. D Functional or engineered uNK cell therapies: Engineered uNK cells secrete factors e. , CSF1, CSF2, CCL5, XCL1 and cytokines IFN- γ, IL-8 , and support vascular remodeling via VEGF and PlGF, aiding trophoblast invasion and spiral artery transformation.

Influence of environmental and maternal factors Environmental and lifestyle factors, including diet, stress, infection, and exposure to toxins, can impact maternal immune function and potentially alter uNK cell behavior 140. However, limited research has focused on how these external factors influence uNK cell function and interactions with trophoblasts 13,22,104. Furthermore, maternal health conditions, such as autoimmune disorders and metabolic syn- dromes, may affect uNK cells and exacerbate pregnancy complications 141. Future studies should explore the environmental and maternal factors affecting uNK cell functions and assess how these influences vary across populations with different genetic backgrounds. Longitudinal changes in uNK cells during pregnancy Most current research on uNK cells is limited to early pregnancy stages, with fewer studies examining their roles in mid-to-late pregnancy 142. Understanding the dynamic changes in uNK cell populations, phenotypes, and functions throughout pregnancy is essential for iden- tifying how they contribute to pregnancy maintenance and how dysre - gulation may lead to complications 143. Longitudinal studies tracking uNK cell characteristics from conception to delivery could reveal crucial insights into their temporal roles and adaptation within the uterine environment 52,104,144. Mechanistic pathways beyond KIR-HLA-C interactions While the KIR-HLA-C axis is well-studied in maternal-fetal tolerance, other molecular pathways may significantly influence uNK cell function 7,145. Pathways involving cytokines like IL-15, IL-10, and TGF-β, as well as non-HLA ligand-receptor interactions, have been suggested to influence uNK cell activity 7,146.

content_chunk: Further research into these less-studied pathways may reveal additional mechanisms that support immune tolerance and placental health, expanding our understanding of the immune microenvironment in pregnancy. Potential for biomarkers and personalized interventions 7. Development of non-invasive biomarkers Identifying biomarkers indicative of uNK cell activity could facilitate early detection of pregnancy complications, such as preeclampsia and recurrent pregnancy loss 21,40. Non-invasive biomarkers, particularly those detectable in maternal blood or urine, would offer clinicians a valuable tool for assessing uNK cell function and associated risks throughout pregnancy 147. Potential biomarkers may include cyto- kines, chemokines, and uNK-specific surface markers that correlate with abnormal immune responses 148. Validation of these biomarkers in large, diverse populations is essential to ensure their reliability and predictive accuracy. Potential for personalized interventions The diversity in uNK cell subtypes and their distinct roles in immune tolerance and placental support suggest a strong potential for person - alized approaches to treating pregnancy complications 149. Person - alized interventions could involve targeted modulation of specific uNK subtypes, or the use of cytokine therapies tailored to an individual s immune profile. For example, regulating cytokines, such as IL-10 or VEGF, based on a patient s specific needs could enhance treatment ef- ficacy by precisely addressing immune imbalances 150. Additionally, genetic screening for KIR-HLA mismatches may help identify women at higher risk for complications, allowing for early, targeted interventions aimed at improving maternal-fetal compatibility 151. Future research should prioritize developing these targeted therapies, focusing on ac- commodating individual variations in immune tolerance mechanisms to maximize therapeutic outcomes 21,152. Personalized approaches offer the promise of more effective, patient-specific care that addresses the unique immune environment of each pregnancy. In summary, advancing our understanding of uNK cells requires a multifaceted approach that includes studies on cellular diversity, environmental impacts, and longitudinal dynamics. Developing reliable biomarkers and personalized therapeutic strategies holds great promise for improving pregnancy outcomes and managing complications linked to uNK dysfunction 153. Bridging these knowledge gaps will be critical for translating basic research on uNK cells into clinical applications, ultimately enhancing maternal-fetal health 36,40. Conclusions and prospects 8. Summary of key insights This review has highlighted the multifaceted role of uNK cells in establishing and maintaining maternal-fetal immune tolerance, ensuring successful placental development, and supporting pregnancy health 7, 53. uNK cells contribute significantly to processes such as trophoblast invasion, spiral artery remodeling, and modulation of immune responses at the maternal-fetal interface 7,13,154. Their interaction with trophoblast cells, mediated through KIR-HLA-C and other molecular pathways, is essential for balancing immune tolerance and defense, thereby preventing adverse pregnancy outcomes 20,27. Additionally, the functional diversity of uNK cell subtypes, characterized by unique cytokine profiles and receptor expressions, underscores the complexity of their regulatory roles 63,77. Understanding the implications of uNK cell dysfunction has provided valuable insights into pregnancy complications, including preeclampsia, recurrent pregnancy loss, and PAS disorders 12,77. Genetic and epigenetic factors that influence uNK cell activity have also emerged as critical determinants of maternal-fetal tolerance, revealing potential risk markers for these conditions 7,55,145.

content_chunk: Advances in research tech- niques, particularly single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial tran- scriptomics, have further enhanced our understanding of uNK cell heterogeneity, opening up new avenues for targeted therapeutic ap- proaches 155. Potential clinical impact and future research The clinical implications of uNK cell research are vast, particularly in developing predictive biomarkers and personalized therapies for preg- nancy complications 104,156. Non-invasive biomarkers reflecting uNK cell activity could transform prenatal care by enabling early detection and intervention for high-risk pregnancies 157. Such bio- markers, combined with genetic screening for KIR-HLA mismatches, may facilitate individualized risk assessments, helping to tailor in- terventions for each patient s unique immunological profile 7,55,66. Future research should focus on exploring uncharted areas in uNK cell biology including their longitudinal behavior across different pregnancy stages and the influence of environmental factors 52,158. These studies could deepen our understanding of how uNK cells adapt to changes within the uterine environment and contribute to pregnancy maintenance over time. Further exploration into alternative ligand-receptor pathways and cytokine interactions will likely reveal additional layers of immune regulation essential for pregnancy health 159. In conclusion, recent advancements in uNK cell research have significantly expanded our understanding of their roles and interactions with trophoblasts 7,22,50,53. Despite remaining gaps in knowledge, these findings highlight the transformative potential of uNK cell research in reproductive immunology and maternal-fetal medicine 160. By continuing to explore molecular mechanisms and the impact of various factors on uNK cell functions, paving the way for innovative diagnostic tools, targeted treatments, and ultimately, improved preg- nancy outcomes. Cytokine modulation and immunoregulation of uterine NK cells in pregnancy disorders Jun Zhoua, Ping Yanb, Wenxue Mac, , Jing Lia, aDepartment of Obstetrics, The Affiliated Hospital of Qingdao University, Qingdao, Shandong 266000, China bQingdao City Health Care Center for Cadres, Qingdao, Shandong 266071, China cDivision of Regenerative Medicine, Department of Medicine, Sanford Stem Cell Institute, University of California San Diego, La Jolla, CA 92093, USA Keywords: Cytokine modulation Growth factor signaling Uterine natural killer uNK cells Immune tolerance KIR-HLA-C interaction Pregnancy complicationsABSTRACT Uterine natural killer uNK cells play a pivotal role in promoting placental development and supporting maternal-fetal immune tolerance, primarily through cytokine regulation and growth factor production. While the importance of uNK cells in pregnancy is well-established, the mechanisms of their interactions with trophoblasts and contributions to various pregnancy complications remain incompletely understood. This review highlights recent advancements in understanding uNK cell functions, with a focus on cytokine production, growth factor secretion, and receptor-ligand interactions, particularly involving killer immunoglobulin-like receptors KIR and human leukocyte antigen-C HLA-C. We explore how uNK cell dysfunction contributes to pregnancy compli - cations, including preeclampsia, recurrent pregnancy loss, and placenta accreta spectrum PAS disorders, emphasizing their roles in immune tolerance and placental health. By detailing the distinct cytokine signaling pathways and functional subtypes of uNK cells, this review provides insights into their regulatory mechanisms essential for pregnancy maintenance. Additionally, we discuss emerging therapeutic strategies targeting uNK- trophoblast interactions and propose future research directions, including the development of non-invasive biomarkers and personalized interventions. This comprehensive review addresses critical knowledge gaps, aiming to advance research in reproductive immunology and guide therapeutic innovations in maternal health. Introduction The placenta is a vital organ that forms during pregnancy, acting as the interface between the mother and the developing fetus 1. It is essential for exchanging nutrients, gases, and waste products, which supports fetal growth and development 2. The placenta comprises various cell types, including trophoblasts, specialized cells derived from the outer layer of the blastocyst 3. Trophoblasts invade the maternal uterine wall to establish the placenta, a process essential for successful pregnancy outcomes 4. Since their identification, uterine natural killer uNK cells have been recognized as key regulators in maintaining maternal-fetal immune tolerance 5. Unlike peripheral NK cells, uNK cells exhibit limited cytotoxicity and are highly adapted to the pregnancy environment, promoting processes such as trophoblast invasion, spiral artery remod - eling, and immune modulation 6. These cells play a crucial role in balancing maternal immune tolerance with immune defense, making them essential players in pregnancy. Recent advances highlight diverse uNK cell subtypes, each with specific roles in supporting fetal develop - ment within the maternal immune environment 7. Placental development involves several key stages, starting with the differentiation of cytotrophoblasts into syncytiotrophoblasts, which form the outer layer of the placenta 8.

In recent years, growing interest has centered on how cytokine and growth factor signaling orchestrates interactions between uNK cells and trophoblasts, with studies revealing that dysregulation of these signals can lead to adverse pregnancy outcomes 13. Advances in single-cell RNA sequencing and proteomics have enabled precise characterization of cytokine expression profiles in uNK cells, identifying key signaling molecules like interleukin-10 IL-10 , transforming growth factor-beta TGF-β , and vascular endothelial growth factor VEGF that play crit- ical roles in immune tolerance and vascular remodeling 14. This expanding knowledge highlights the potential of cytokine modulation as a therapeutic strategy for managing pregnancy complications linked to uNK cell dysfunction. For instance, certain combinations of maternal KIR and fetal HLA-C genotypes are linked to a higher likelihood of developing pre- eclampsia, highlighting the potential for genetic predispositions to impact uNK cell function and pregnancy outcomes 17. Despite recent advances, comprehensive studies across diverse populations are needed to confirm these associations and improve generalizability 18. This article provides a comprehensive synthesis of recent advance - ments in understanding the roles of uNK cells in placental development and pregnancy outcomes 7,19.

content_chunk: It examines distinct uNK cell subtypes, cytokine production, and their interactions with trophoblasts, primarily through KIR-HLA-C engagement 7,20 , to illuminate the mechanisms by which uNK cells influence maternal-fetal immune tolerance and pregnancy health. Additionally, it explores the association of uNK cell dysfunction with pregnancy complications and the potential of thera - peutic strategies targeting uNK-trophoblast interactions 21. This exploration serves as a bridge between basic research and clinical ap- plications, guiding future studies on therapeutic interventions and biomarker development. This article is structured to provide a comprehensive understanding of uNK cells within the broader context of maternal-fetal immune tolerance 5,7,11. It begins by reviewing foundational mechanisms of immune tolerance during pregnancy, including key cellular and mo- lecular players involved 22. Following this, the specific functions of uNK cells are explored, with an emphasis on their subtypes and roles in supporting placental development 12,23. The potential impacts of uNK cell dysfunction on pregnancy complications are then discussed, including associated mechanisms and genetic predispositions 11. Emerging techniques, such as single-cell RNA sequencing, are high- lighted for their contributions to advancing our understanding of uNK cell heterogeneity 21,24. Finally, the manuscript examines current and prospective therapeutic strategies targeting uNK cell functions and concludes with a summary of key insights and future research directions in this field 7,25. In summary, studying placental immune interactions, particularly the role of uNK cells, is crucial for understanding and managing preg- nancy outcomes 7,11. Recent advances have provided significant in- sights into these interactions, highlighting their complexity and importance 7,26,27. This review aims to synthesize current knowledge, identify gaps, and suggest future research directions, mak- ing a valuable contribution to reproductive immunology and maternal-fetal medicine 11,28. Maternal-fetal immune tolerances Achieving immune tolerance at the maternal-fetal interface is essential for a successful pregnancy, requiring a finely tuned balance between immune defense and tolerance 22,29. This section explores the key components and processes that establish and maintain this balance, beginning with an overview of the immune tolerance mecha - nisms in place during pregnancy 30. Overview of immune tolerance mechanisms The establishment and maintenance of immune tolerance at the maternal-fetal interface are critical for a successful pregnancy. Maternal immune tolerance involves a complex interplay of cellular and molec - ular components that allow the maternal immune system to accept the semi-allogeneic fetus while preserving the ability to defend against in- fections 31. A key player in this process is the uNK cell, which, unlike peripheral NK cells, exhibits reduced cytotoxicity and is adapted to promote tolerance and support placental development 12,13,32. Additionally, other immune cells, including macrophages, dendritic cells DCs , and T regulatory cells Tregs , contribute to a balanced immune environment that facilitates fetal development 33. Each of these cell types produces cytokines, growth factors, and other mediators that support the delicate balance between immune tolerance and de- fense within the uterine environment 34. Molecular mechanisms of tolerance At the molecular level, several key signaling pathways are involved in establishing maternal-fetal immune tolerance 35. One prominent pathway involves the interaction between KIRs on uNK cells and HLA-C molecules on trophoblasts 16,27,36. This KIR-HLA-C engagement plays a pivotal role in regulating trophoblast invasion and promoting immune tolerance 20,22,32. Certain combinations of maternal KIR and fetal HLA-C genotypes have been associated with more favorable pregnancy outcomes, while others may predispose to complications such as preeclampsia 18,37. Cytokine signaling is another crucial mechanism in immune toler- ance at the maternal-fetal interface 38. uNK cells, along with other immune cells in the decidua, produce cytokines like interleukin-10 IL-10 and transforming growth factor-beta TGF-β , which are essen - tial for maintaining an anti-inflammatory environment conducive to pregnancy 39,40. IL-10 helps suppress pro-inflammatory responses that could harm the fetus, while TGF-β contributes to immune regulation by modulating the function of uNK cells and Tregs 41. These cytokines collectively foster a supportive environment that minimizes maternal immune attacks on fetal cells while enabling immune adaptations that support fetal growth 42. To further illustrate the temporal changes in immune regulation essential for pregnancy, Fig. 2provides an overview of immune cell dynamics across the trimesters, emphasizing the shifts from an initial pro-inflammatory state to an anti-inflammatory phase and finally returning to a pro-inflammatory environment as pregnancy progresses 43. These phases reflect the intricate balance required at the maternal-fetal interface to support implantation, fetal development, and preparation for labor 44. Cytokine and Growth Factor Reviews 81 2025 40 53 422. Role of trophoblasts in tolerance Trophoblasts, specialized cells originating from the outer layer of the blastocyst, play a direct role in immune tolerance at the maternal-fetal interface 22,29,45. These cells differentiate into extravillous tropho - blasts EVTs , which invade the maternal decidua and interact with uNK cells and other maternal immune cells 7,13,46. EVTs express non-classical HLA molecules, including HLA-G, which interacts with inhibitory receptors on uNK cells and Tregs to promote immune toler- ance 47. By doing so, trophoblasts help modulate local immune re- sponses, ensuring that the maternal immune system does not mount an attack against fetal cells while facilitating the necessary remodeling of spiral arteries for optimal placental function 48,49. In summary, maternal-fetal immune tolerance is mediated by a network of immune cells, signaling pathways, and cellular interactions at the maternal-fetal interface. uNK cells, through KIR-HLA-C in- teractions and cytokine production, along with the regulatory functions of trophoblasts, play central roles in maintaining this tolerance 13,20, 27,50. Understanding these mechanisms is crucial for identifying how disruptions in tolerance may lead to pregnancy complications and for developing therapeutic approaches to mitigate these risks 16,18,39. Cellular and molecular mechanisms of uNK cells in pregnancy uNK cells play a critical role in pregnancy by modulating key pro- cesses that support placental development and maternal-fetal immune tolerance 5,51,52.

CD56brightCD16dim uNK cells This subtype represents the majority of uNK cells in the decidua during early pregnancy and is primarily responsible for cytokine and growth factor production rather than direct cytotoxicity 55,56. CD56bright uNK cells secrete immunomodulatory cytokines, such as interleukin-10 IL-10 and transforming growth factor-beta TGF- β , which promote an immune-tolerant environment 22,40,57. However, their activity in the decidua is modulated to prevent excessive aggression towards fetal cells 12,59. CD56dim uNK cells may contribute to immune surveillance, acting as a defense mechanism against potential infections during pregnancy 60. How- ever, their role remains more restrained, focusing on regulatory functions and maintaining a balanced immune response 39,58.

KIR-HLA-C interactions The engagement of killer immunoglobulin-like receptors KIRs on uNK cells with human leukocyte antigen-C HLA-C on trophoblasts is central to regulating trophoblast invasion and maintaining maternal- fetal tolerance 11,63,64. Specific combinations of maternal KIR and fetal HLA-C alleles influence the extent of trophoblast invasion and are associated with various pregnancy outcomes 22. or instance, certain KIR-HLA-C genotypes promote a more invasive trophoblast phenotype, facilitating deeper placental embedding and improved vascular adap- tation. Conversely, mismatches in these genotypes can lead to inade - quate uNK-trophoblast interactions, contributing to complications such as preeclampsia and recurrent pregnancy loss 65,66. This interaction underscores the importance of genetic compatibility in promoting optimal uNK cell function during pregnancy. Cytokine signaling pathways uNK cells secrete various cytokines that influence trophoblast behavior and modulate immune responses within the decidua 7,22,63. Key cytokines, such as interferon-gamma IFN- γ , interleukin-8 IL-8 , and interleukin-10 IL-10 , play dual roles in regulating immune toler- ance and promoting placental development. IFN- γ, released by uNK cells, plays a critical role in regulating trophoblast invasion and pro- moting spiral artery remodeling, primarily through pathways involving nitric oxide and prostaglandin signaling 67. This cytokine supports vascular changes necessary for adequate placental function. Addition - ally, IL-8 and IL-10 are essential for creating an environment that bal- ances trophoblast invasion with immune tolerance, which is vital for healthy placental development 48,68.

Growth factors and angiogenic signaling The production of growth factors by uNK cells, such as vascular endothelial growth factor VEGF and placental growth factor PlGF , is essential for promoting angiogenesis and vascular remodeling 69. These growth factors facilitate the transformation of spiral arteries, ensuring an increased blood supply to the developing fetus 70. Both VEGF and PlGF are pivotal for vascular remodeling processes, promoting the structural adaptation of blood vessels to support placental and fetal growth, and their presence ensures adequate placental perfusion by stimulating angiogenesis. Additionally, uNK cells express angiopoietins, which contribute to vascular stability and maturation, further support - ing the development of a robust maternal-fetal circulation 12,13,71. Through these cellular and molecular mechanisms, uNK cells exert multifaceted effects that are essential for a successful pregnancy 7,40, 53. The diversity in uNK cell subtypes and their signaling interactions highlights the complexity of immune regulation at the maternal-fetal interface 72. Further understanding of these pathways could provide insights into therapeutic strategies for managing pregnancy-related complications. Pregnancy complications linked to uNK dysfunction Aberrations in uNK cell function have been implicated in several pregnancy complications, with dysfunctional uNK cells contributing to impaired placental development and inadequate maternal-fetal immune tolerance 5,73. This section explores specific pregnancy disorders associated with uNK dysfunction, detailing molecular mechanisms, and the impact of genetic and epigenetic factors on uNK cell function 7,74. Detailed mechanisms 4. Preeclampsia Preeclampsia is a complex pregnancy disorder characterized by high blood pressure and end-organ damage, affecting both maternal and fetal health 75,76.
